questions.q: The employees were asked to comply ____ the new safety rules.
questions.x: 'Comply with' is the correct preposition.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: UNANIMOUS
questions.x: 'Unanimous' is the opposite of 'Divided'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Unanimous'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Zeal'.
questions.x: 'Zeal' means enthusiasm. 'Apathy' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
She did not / knew the answer / to the question.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'knew the answer'. After 'did not', use the base form: 'know'.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Deteriorate'.
questions.x: 'Deteriorate' is the opposite of 'Improve'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Deteriorate'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The news / are / very encouraging.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'are'. 'News' is singular: 'is'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To be in the same boat'
o: To be in the same difficult situation
questions.x: 'To be in the same boat' means: to be in the same difficult situation.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To kill two birds with one stone'
o: To achieve two aims with a single action
questions.x: 'To kill two birds with one stone' means: to achieve two aims with a single action.

The furnitures in the new office / were supplied / by a local firm.
o: The furnitures in the new office
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'The furnitures in the new office'. 'Furniture' is uncountable: 'The furniture … was supplied'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'Something that is no longer in use'
questions.x: 'Obsolete' means something that is no longer in use.

questions.q: Who are described as bearing the brunt of heat waves?
questions.x: Answer: 'Outdoor workers'. The passage lists construction labourers, street vendors and delivery riders. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Every year, heat waves arrive a little earlier and stay a little longer. Outdoor workers — construction labourers, street vendors, delivery riders — bear the brunt. Simple measures such as shaded rest areas, drinking water and shifting heavy work to cooler hours can save lives. Some cities have prepared heat action plans that issue alerts and open cooling centres. What was once considered a seasonal discomfort is now recognised as an occupational hazard.

questions.q: The last sentence suggests that heat waves are now seen as:
o: A risk to workers' safety and health at work
questions.x: Answer: 'A risk to workers' safety and health at work'. It calls heat an 'occupational hazard'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Every year, heat waves arrive a little earlier and stay a little longer. Outdoor workers — construction labourers, street vendors, delivery riders — bear the brunt. Simple measures such as shaded rest areas, drinking water and shifting heavy work to cooler hours can save lives. Some cities have prepared heat action plans that issue alerts and open cooling centres. What was once considered a seasonal discomfort is now recognised as an occupational hazard.

questions.q: The 1917 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Annie Besant, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Calcutta; it was the first session presided over by a woman.

questions.q: The newspaper/journal 'Young India (as editor from 1919)' is associated with:
o: Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
questions.x: 'Young India (as editor from 1919)' was started/edited by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 30 January 1948. 30 January is observed as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas).

questions.q: Who founded the 'Harijan Sevak Sangh' in 1932?
questions.x: Correct answer: Mahatma Gandhi. Gandhi formed it after the Poona Pact to work against untouchability.

questions.q: Who founded the Indian Independence League (East Asia)?
o: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru
questions.x: The Indian Independence League (East Asia) was founded by Rash Behari Bose.

questions.q: Who among the following co-founded the Women's Indian Association (1917) with Annie Besant?
questions.x: Correct answer: Margaret Cousins. The Women's Indian Association was founded at Adyar in 1917.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: the Non-Cooperation Movement was formally launched.
questions.x: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally launched in 1920. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Wood's Despatch (1854), called the 'Magna Carta of English education in India', was issued during the tenure of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Dalhousie. It led to universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1857.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were executed.
questions.x: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were executed in 1931. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Ilbert Bill controversy (1883)?
questions.x: Lord Ripon was Viceroy during the Ilbert Bill controversy (1883).

questions.q: The 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme was launched in 2015 at:
questions.x: Correct answer: Panipat, Haryana. It addresses the declining child sex ratio.

questions.q: The 'World Development Report' is published by:
questions.x: 'World Development Report' is brought out by World Bank.

questions.q: The military exercise 'SIMBEX' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'SIMBEX' is a bilateral exercise between India and Singapore.

questions.q: Which company is setting up India's first commercial semiconductor fab at Dholera, Gujarat, in partnership with Taiwan's PSMC?
questions.x: The Dholera, Gujarat fab is a joint effort with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 22 December?
o: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (Sardar Patel's birth anniversary)
National Statistics Day (birth anniversary of P. C. Mahalanobis)
questions.x: 22 December is National Mathematics Day (Srinivasa Ramanujan).

questions.q: Human Rights Day is observed on:
questions.x: Human Rights Day: 10 December.

questions.q: The 'Swachh Survekshan' is published by:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.x: 'Swachh Survekshan' is brought out by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

questions.q: Manu Bhaker became the first Indian after independence to win two medals at a single Olympics. Her second medal at Paris 2024 came in:
o: 10 m air pistol mixed team with Sarabjot Singh
questions.x: Correct answer: 10 m air pistol mixed team with Sarabjot Singh. Her first was the individual 10 m air pistol bronze.

questions.q: The 'PM-eBus Sewa' scheme aims to:
o: Provide free bus passes to students
Deploy electric buses in cities on a PPP model
questions.x: Correct answer: Deploy electric buses in cities on a PPP model. It supports 10,000 e-buses in cities.

questions.q: The headquarters of the UNICEF is located in:
questions.x: UNICEF: headquartered in New York.

questions.q: The Constitution (100th Amendment) Act, 2015:
o: Reserved one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
Gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (exchange of enclaves)
Added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble and inserted Fundamental Duties
Extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures and ended nomination of Anglo-Indian members
questions.x: The 100th Amendment (2015) gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (exchange of enclaves).

questions.q: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated on 2 October 1959 at:
questions.x: Correct answer: Nagaur, Rajasthan. Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated it at Nagaur.

questions.q: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains:
o: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes
Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
questions.x: Seventh Schedule: Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Protection of life and personal liberty"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 21.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Organisation of village panchayats"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 40.

questions.q: How many Union Territories does India have at present?
questions.x: Delhi, J&K, Ladakh, Chandigarh, Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar, and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Failure of constitutional machinery in States (President's Rule)"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 356.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Joint sitting of both Houses in certain cases"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 108.

questions.q: The 'creamy layer' concept for OBC reservations was laid down in:
o: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
M. R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963)
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951)
questions.x: The Court upheld 27% OBC reservation, excluding the creamy layer, and capped total reservation at 50% ordinarily.

questions.q: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as per the Constitution is:
questions.x: 238 elected representatives of States/UTs plus 12 nominated by the President.

questions.q: The Narasimham Committee (1991, 1998) is associated with:
o: Economic capital framework of the RBI
questions.x: Narasimham Committee (1991, 1998): Banking sector reforms.

questions.q: The 'One District One Product' (ODOP) initiative aims to:
o: Promote a distinctive product from each district for balanced regional development
questions.x: Correct answer: Promote a distinctive product from each district for balanced regional development. It began in Uttar Pradesh and was scaled nationally.

questions.q: FDI is distinguished from FPI mainly by:
o: The intention of lasting interest and management control (typically 10% or more equity)
questions.x: Correct answer: The intention of lasting interest and management control (typically 10% or more equity). FPI is portfolio investment without control.

questions.q: 'Core inflation' excludes the prices of:
questions.x: Food and fuel are volatile; core inflation reflects underlying trends.

questions.q: In an economy, GDP at market prices is ₹3,22,000 crore, net factor income from abroad is ₹-900 crore and depreciation is ₹17,000 crore. NNP at market prices is:
The 'Basel norms' relate to:
o: Capital adequacy and risk management of banks
questions.x: Correct answer: Capital adequacy and risk management of banks. Basel III strengthened capital and liquidity requirements.

questions.q: An IPO refers to:
o: The first sale of shares by a company to the public
questions.x: Correct answer: The first sale of shares by a company to the public. Subsequent public offers are called FPOs.

questions.q: When demand for a commodity is perfectly inelastic, the demand curve is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Vertical. Quantity demanded does not change with price.

questions.q: The Human Development Index is published by:
questions.x: HDI combines life expectancy, education (mean and expected years of schooling) and GNI per capita.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over:
o: Revenue receipts plus non-debt capital receipts
questions.x: Correct answer: Revenue receipts plus non-debt capital receipts. It indicates total borrowing requirements of the government.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹49,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹2,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹5,500. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹49,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 2,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 5,500
Pass book balance = ₹46,000.

questions.q: A debtor becomes insolvent and nothing can be recovered. The entry is:
o: Provision A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Bad Debts A/c Dr. To Debtor's A/c
Debtor's A/c Dr. To Bad Debts A/c
Bad Debts A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
questions.x: Correct answer: Bad Debts A/c Dr. To Debtor's A/c. The irrecoverable amount is written off as a loss.

questions.q: The Trading Account is prepared to ascertain:
questions.x: It records sales, purchases, opening/closing stock and direct expenses.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹2,000 at the end of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 12% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 2,000 = ₹24,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the end of each month = 5.5 months.
Interest = 24,000 × 12% × 5.5/12 = ₹1,320.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,05,000, selling price is ₹175 per unit and variable cost is ₹150 per unit. The break-even point in units is:
questions.x:
Contribution per unit = 175 − 150 = ₹25.
BEP (units) = Fixed cost / Contribution per unit = 1,05,000 / 25 = 4,200 units.

questions.q: Depreciation is best described as:
o: Creation of a fund for replacing assets
Allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life
A process of valuation of assets at market price
questions.x: Depreciation is an allocation of cost, a non-cash expense; it is not a valuation process.

questions.q: A business has total assets of ₹1,20,000 and outside liabilities of ₹35,000. Its capital (owner's equity) is:
questions.x: Assets = Liabilities + Capital → Capital = 1,20,000 − 35,000 = ₹85,000.

questions.q: Net sales are ₹6,90,000 and the cost of goods sold is ₹4,14,000. The gross profit ratio is:
questions.x:
Gross profit = 6,90,000 − 4,14,000 = ₹2,76,000.
GP ratio = GP / Net sales × 100 = 40%. (Dividing by COGS gives mark-up, not GP ratio.)

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹2,10,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 2 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 2,10,000 × (0.9)^2 = ₹1,70,100.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,68,000.)

questions.q: When shares are forfeited, the share capital account is debited with the:
o: Amount called up on those shares
questions.x: Amount received is credited to Share Forfeiture A/c; unpaid calls are credited to calls account.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 3 : 1. They admit R for a 1/8 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
The debt–equity ratio measures:
o: Long-term solvency and the mix of borrowed and owned funds
questions.x: Correct answer: Long-term solvency and the mix of borrowed and owned funds. It compares long-term debt with shareholders' funds.

questions.q: The accrual basis of accounting records revenues and expenses:
o: Only when cash is received or paid
When they are earned or incurred, regardless of cash receipt or payment
Only at the end of the business's life
questions.x: Accrual accounting is mandatory for companies under the Companies Act, 2013.

questions.q: The process of transferring entries from the journal to the ledger is called:
questions.x: Posting is followed by balancing of accounts.

questions.q: Equal remuneration provisions under the Code on Wages prohibit discrimination on the ground of gender. Here 'gender' expressly includes:
questions.x: Section 3 bars discrimination on the ground of gender, including transgender identity, in wages and in recruitment for the same or similar work.

questions.q: The OSH Code generally applies to establishments employing at least:
questions.x: The general applicability is 10 or more workers; mines and docks are covered regardless of the number employed.

questions.q: Article 43A, directing the State to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries, was inserted by:
questions.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Article 43A to the Directive Principles.

questions.q: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 came into force on:
questions.x: The ID Act came into force on 1 April 1947, before Independence.

questions.q: The Code that requires a 'national database' for inter-State migrant workers and unorganised workers along with Aadhaar-based registration is primarily:
o: The OSH Code read with the Code on Social Security
questions.x: Database provisions appear in the OSH Code (migrant workers) and the Code on Social Security (unorganised workers via self-registration).

questions.q: Identify the year of enactment of the Payment of Gratuity Act.
questions.x: The Payment of Gratuity Act was enacted in 1972.

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, 'weekly holiday' for a worker means:
o: No weekly rest if paid extra
At least one day of rest in a week, ordinarily Sunday or a substituted day
Two days off every week compulsorily
A rest day once a month
questions.x: Workers must get a weekly day off; substitution is allowed under conditions so that no worker works more than ten days continuously without a holiday.

questions.q: Which kind of employment did the IR Code formally recognise across all sectors, giving such workers the same wages and benefits as permanent workers?
questions.x: Fixed-term employment is recognised; such workers get the same hours, wages, allowances and benefits as permanent workers doing similar work.

questions.q: Representation of workers on the Board of Directors of a company is known as:
questions.x: Board-level participation is the highest form of workers' participation in management.

questions.q: Who is the Director-General of the ILO who assumed office in October 2022?
questions.x: Gilbert Houngbo of Togo, the first African DG, succeeded Guy Ryder in 2022.

questions.q: CPI for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) and Rural Labourers (CPI-RL) are used mainly to:
o: Revise minimum wages for agricultural workers and MGNREGA wage rates
questions.x: CPI-AL is used for revising minimum wages in agriculture and MGNREGA wage rates are indexed to it.

questions.q: Which of the four Labour Codes was the first to receive Presidential assent?
o: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code
questions.x: The Code on Wages received assent in August 2019; the other three Codes were passed in September 2020.

questions.q: Maslow's hierarchy of needs places which need at the top?
questions.x: From bottom: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation.

questions.q: Which Act of 1948 was the first major social insurance law of independent India?
questions.x: The ESI Act, 1948 introduced integrated health and cash benefits; the scheme was first implemented at Kanpur and Delhi in February 1952.

questions.q:
Match the law with the Code into which it was merged:
Old law:
A. Minimum Wages Act, 1948
B. Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
C. Maternity Benefit Act, 1961
D. Factories Act, 1948
Code:
1. Industrial Relations Code
2. Code on Wages
3. OSH Code
4. Code on Social Security
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Minimum Wages Act, 1948) → 2 (Code on Wages); B (Industrial Disputes Act, 1947) → 1 (Industrial Relations Code); C (Maternity Benefit Act, 1961) → 4 (Code on Social Security); D (Factories Act, 1948) → 3 (OSH Code).
Minimum Wages → Code on Wages; ID Act → IR Code; Maternity Benefit → Code on Social Security; Factories → OSH Code.

questions.q: A 'job description' documents:
o: The duties, responsibilities and working conditions of a job
The salary history of the incumbent
The qualifications of the ideal candidate
questions.x: Job description describes the job; job specification describes the person (skills, qualifications).

questions.q: The agency implementing PM-JAY at the national level is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: National Health Authority. NHA implements PM-JAY and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.

questions.q: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund is administered separately because:
o: It is governed by a State law covering tea plantation workers in Assam
questions.x: Assam tea plantation workers are covered by a separate State PF scheme.

questions.q: A working journalist becomes eligible for gratuity after continuous service of:
questions.x: Working journalists have a reduced qualifying period of three years.

questions.q: When the EPF scheme began in 1952, it initially covered how many industries?
questions.x: Initially six industries were covered — cement, cigarettes, electrical/mechanical/general engineering, iron and steel, paper and textiles.

questions.q: NPS was opened to all citizens of India on a voluntary basis from:
questions.x: The 'All Citizens Model' was launched on 1 May 2009.

questions.q: 'Portability' of social security benefits means:
o: Benefits can be carried across jobs and locations without loss
Benefits are paid only to permanent workers
Benefits are paid in cash only
questions.x: UAN-based EPF portability and One Nation One Ration Card are examples.

questions.q: The UMANG app is used by EPF members to:
o: Access EPFO services such as passbook view, claim filing and UAN activation
questions.x: UMANG integrates many government services, including EPFO's member services.

questions.q: The wage ceiling for coverage under the ESI Act since 1 January 2017 is:
questions.x: Correct answer: ₹21,000 per month. The ceiling is ₹21,000 a month (₹25,000 for persons with disability).

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹13,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹8,000 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 8.33%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 8,000) = ₹8,000.
Salary for computation = min(13,500, 8,000) = ₹8,000.
Annual bonus = 8,000 × 12 × 8.33% = ₹7,997. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: EPF stands for:
questions.x: EPF is a compulsory savings scheme for retirement under the EPF & MP Act, 1952.

questions.q: A member who opts for early pension under EPS 1995 at age 55 suffers a reduction of how much for each year short of 58?
questions.x: Early pension (from 50) is reduced by 4% for every year the age falls short of 58; deferred pension up to 60 earns 4% per year more.

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹10,500 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹78.75 → ₹79; employer share 3.25% = ₹341.25 → ₹342 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹421 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Artificial Intelligence'?
questions.x: Artificial Intelligence is abbreviated as AI.

questions.q: Ctrl + C is used to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Copy the selected item. Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + V pastes.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Internet Protocol'?
questions.x: Internet Protocol is abbreviated as IP (address).

questions.q: The gas used in the manufacture of vanaspati ghee by hydrogenation of oils is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Hydrogen. Nickel acts as a catalyst.

questions.q: A 'light year' is a unit of:
questions.x: It is the distance light travels in one year (~9.46 × 10¹² km).

questions.q: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.x: Correct answer: 3 × 10⁸ m/s. 340 m/s is roughly the speed of sound in air.

questions.q: Plants absorb water mainly through:
questions.x: Correct answer: Root hairs. Water moves up through xylem; food moves through phloem.

questions.q: Aadhaar authentication and UPI are examples of India's:
questions.x: Correct answer: Digital public infrastructure. India Stack is a set of such digital public goods.

questions.q: The SI unit of potential difference is the:
questions.x: Potential difference is measured in Volts.

questions.q: Electromagnetic induction is credited to:
questions.x: Electromagnetic induction: Michael Faraday.

questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Skin. The liver is the largest internal organ (and largest gland).

questions.q: The SI unit of amount of substance is the:
questions.x: Amount of substance is measured in Moles.

questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 4?
questions.x:
Total outcomes = 36. Pairs with sum 4: (1,3), (2,2), (3,1) → 3.
P = 3/36 = 1/12.

questions.q: A trader buys a bicycle for ₹1,050 and sells it for ₹1,134. His profit per cent is:
questions.x:
Profit = SP − CP = ₹1,134 − ₹1,050 = ₹84.
Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (84 / 1,050) × 100 = 8%.
(Profit % is always on cost price, not on selling price.)

questions.q: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 2:10?
questions.x:
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30×2 − 5.5×10| = |60 − 55| = 5°.
Smaller angle = 5°.
(The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute over the hour hand.)

questions.q: A rectangular plot measures 55 m by 34 m. What is the cost of fencing it at ₹30 per metre?
In a certain code language, POLICY is written as NMJGAW. How is INCOME written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare POLICY → NMJGAW: P→N, O→M, L→J…
Rule: each letter is moved 2 places backward in the alphabet.
Applying it to INCOME gives GLAMKC.

questions.q: In a line of trainees, Rahul is 23rd from the front and 30th from the back. How many persons are there in all?
questions.x: Total = (position from front) + (position from back) − 1 = 23 + 30 − 1 = 52. Rahul is counted in both positions, hence −1.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of 3^115?
questions.x:
Unit digit depends only on 3. Powers of 3 repeat with cycle 4: 3, 9, 7, 1.
115 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 3 → use position 3 of the cycle → 7.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a storage tank in 24 hours and 40 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 60 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(24, 40, 60) = 120 units.
Rates: +5, +3, −2 units/hour → net 6 units/hour.
Time = 120 / 6 = 20 hours.

questions.q: The average weight of 15 parcels is 37 kg. When one more parcel is added, the average becomes 40 kg. The weight of the new parcel is:
questions.x:
Old total = 15 × 37 = 555 kg. New total = 16 × 40 = 640 kg.
New parcel = 640 − 555 = 85 kg.
Shortcut: new value = new average + (increase × old count) = 40 + 3 × 15 = 85 kg.

questions.q: In what ratio must coffee seeds costing ₹100 per kg be mixed with coffee seeds costing ₹160 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹146 per kg?
questions.x:
Alligation: (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper) = (160 − 146) : (146 − 100) = 14 : 46 = 7 : 23.
This is cheaper : dearer.

questions.q: What simple interest will ₹19,000 earn in 5 years at 12% per annum?
If 22 June of a certain year falls on a Sunday, on which day of the week will 19 December of the same year fall?
questions.x:
Days from 22 June to 19 December = 180 = 25 weeks + 5 odd days.
Sunday + 5 = Friday. (February is not involved, so leap years do not matter.)

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 107, 63, 97 and 59.
questions.x: 59, 97, 107 are all prime numbers; 63 is not. Hence 63 is the odd one out.

questions.q: Ravi can digitise a set of records in 30 days and Kiran can do it in 70 days. Working together, they will finish it in:
questions.x:
One day's work: 1/30 + 1/70 = 100/2100 = 1/21.
Together they need 21 days. (Product/Sum: 30×70/(30+70) = 21.)
